findings.evidence: lean_source.py:291 `if opener == "(" and colon is not None:` — the filter is on the delimiter, with no dot-notation condition; module docstring lines 8-9 claim the module carries no lint policy.
findings.fix: State the mechanical contract: only explicit parenthesized `(x : α)` binders are returned; implicit `{}`/`⦃⦄` and instance-implicit `[]` binders are skipped. Keep the dot-notation justification in `lint-dot-notation.py`, and drop "for receiver matching" from `VariableBinding`.
findings.issue: `variable_bindings` explains its omission as "Implicit and instance-implicit variables are intentionally omitted because they cannot be dot-notation receivers" — lint policy copied unadapted into a module whose own docstring (lines 8-9) says it exists "so later hygiene checks can reuse the parser without importing lint policy". A new consumer reads the reason as inapplicable to it, though the omission is unconditional. Same leak in `VariableBinding` at line 60 ("for receiver matching").

findings.evidence: lean_source.py:200-213: `if text.startswith(":=", header_end) and depth == 0: break` … `return tuple(binders), text[start:header_end]` — the returned slice ends before `:=`.
findings.fix: Reword to "the header up to, but excluding, ``:=``, ``where``, or the first equation bar", and fix the identical wording in `_declaration_tail`'s docstring (line 185).
findings.issue: `Declaration`'s docstring says the field is "header through its body introducer", but `_declaration_tail` cuts the slice at the introducer: `header_end` stops on `:=`/`where`/`|` and returns `text[start:header_end]`, so `:=` is not included. `declarations` (line 233) documents the same field correctly as "up to ``:=``, ``where``, or an equation clause", so the two contradict.

summary: The new module and its public declarations are documented, but two docstrings are inaccurate: the section-variable docs justify a general parser limitation with dot-notation lint policy in a module that claims to be policy-free, and the Declaration docstring describes the header as including the body introducer when it excludes it.
